title: Carving stories at their natural joints.
title_zh: 在自然节点上雕刻故事
abstract: Over the past three decades, psychology has documented the recurrence of specific themes in stories across cultures (e.g., love, alliances, monsters, and imaginary worlds) and linked them to identifiable motivational mechanisms (e.g., mate choice, cooperation, threat detection, and exploration). Yet this body of work has remained fragmented, organized around individual themes rather than integrated into a unified account of what makes narrative content psychologically engaging. Here, we propose the Motivational-Ingredient Framework. We identify a set of motivational ingredients: core narrative features, each defined by the specific motivational mechanism it activates. Drawing on evolutionary psychology, affective neuroscience, and the study of human motivation, we compile a comprehensive table of ingredients grounded in the current understanding of human motivational architecture. This framework offers a theory-driven, cross-culturally applicable foundation for the empirical study of narrative content, with implications for fields ranging from media psychology and computational humanities to education and public policy. abstract_zh: 在过去三十年里，心理学记录了跨文化故事中某些主题的反复出现（例如爱情、联盟、怪物和想象世界），并将其与可识别的动机机制联系起来（如配偶选择、合作、威胁检测和探索）。然而，这一研究领域仍然碎片化，围绕单个主题组织，而非整合成关于叙事内容为何在心理上具有吸引力的统一解释。本文提出了动机成分框架（Motivational-Ingredient Framework）。我们识别了一组动机成分：核心叙事特征，每个特征由其激活的特定动机机制定义。借鉴进化心理学、情感神经科学和人类动机研究，我们编制了一张基于当前人类动机架构理解的综合成分表。该框架为叙事内容的经验研究提供了一个理论驱动、跨文化适用的基础，并对媒体心理学、计算人文学、教育和公共政策等领域具有启示意义。（PsycInfo 数据库记录（c）2026 APA，保留所有权利）
